result.decision_rationale:
The required focused gate passed at the candidate. Two source defects still block S05. Automatic selection can replace the rider brain’s reachable target with an unreachable one. A travel restriction can also cause an invalid target to be reported as an ordinary cancellation.

## Continuation for Claude

For R8-F1, apply the native action-range and sight requirements before an alternative can replace the brain’s proposal. For R8-F2, give an unreleased wrapper’s target invalidation precedence over retirement for failed stationary geometry, including at queued promotion. Keep both corrections within the existing rider-brain and exact-wrapper paths. Preserve manual selection, valid stationary strikes, player overrides and native completion of released attacks.

The requested evidence is a production-path comparison of the two equal-ranked targets and an observer-order comparison for a still-remembered invalid target. Use the existing focused gate on any authorized successor. Round 8 reaches the recorded PR-1 review ceiling. Further formal review requires owner direction.

findings.actual: ResolveEqualRankTie marks A ineligible because it is disliked. It accepts B on cached sight alone because pair travel is unrestricted. Both targets have the same distance-derived negative weight. Choose gives the ineligible proposal an infinite distance to beat and selects B. Final proposal admission permits approach to B.
findings.blocking_rationale: An idle pair can pursue a target the native brain has already marked unreachable while a reachable hostile is available.
findings.expected: A remains the target. Native scoring discounts a disliked target but still permits it. A target marked unreachable must already be in native action range and in sight.
findings.requested_correction: Apply native action-range admission together with cached sight wherever the native action requires both. Preserve the valid in-range unreachable case and the stationary mounted-strike check.
findings.requested_evidence: Drive ObserveAutomaticProposal with the two equal-distance, out-of-range targets. Record that A owns the order and B receives no dispatch or carrier. Retain an in-range, in-sight control and the blocked stationary-proposal cases.
findings.title: An unreachable enemy can replace the brain’s reachable proposal
findings.trigger: A mobile real-time melee pair has two equally distant remembered enemies outside attack range. Native proposes reachable A, its DislikedTarget. B is in UnreachableUnits and has cached line of sight.

findings.actual: Group memory still contains the target, so the perception check returns. The drive then calls TryRetireStockIntent before validating the target. Failed stationary geometry retires the wrapper for 'hold out of reach' with Cancelled and CommandCancelled. The wrapper’s own tick checks target validity first and records TargetInvalid. Queued promotion also calls the geometry-first retirement path.

findings.expected: Either observer retires the unreleased wrapper with TargetInvalid, the reason that the target became unconscious, and zero further movement or spending.
findings.requested_correction: Check the exact unreleased wrapper’s target validity before retiring it solely for failed stationary geometry. Apply that ordering to the drive and queued promotion. Keep the existing retirement for a valid target that moves out of reach.
findings.requested_evidence: Keep the target in group memory and compare controller-first and wrapper-first observation after it becomes unconscious outside stationary reach. Assert cause, bounded reason, rejection code, movement and spending. Exercise the same condition at queued promotion and retain a valid out-of-reach control.

prior_finding_assessments.rationale: The patch observes the click handler’s sole ManualTarget setter and reports the combat state actually written. The recorded harness clears the old assignment after an unrelated non-writing Run and preserves the rider’s assignment when the cannot-attack router consumes the rider submission. Genuine same-target, skipped, simulated and unhandled click controls passed.

The harness forwards ordinary versus single-attack mode, supplies the modeled natural weapon and slot, and executes production plan validation and OnEnded. The ordinary horse routine completed 2/2 on A with one Standard spent. Valid B received one dispatch and invalid B received zero. Dismount stopped the routine after one delivery, and the explicit single control completed 1/1.

The harness supplies the CanAct observation through the production force-finish and running-interrupt hooks, then uses production actor evaluation. Across the full observation window, both branches recorded zero rider resubmissions. An eligible horse received one submission and delivered two modeled attacks with zero warnings. Spent and ended horses received zero submissions and produced one rider refusal.

For the reported despawn with simultaneous removal from group memory, the controller now asks the wrapper whether its target is invalid before cancelling for perception loss. Gate rows 1980–1988 record matching TargetInvalid cause, despawn reason and rejection code, with zero movement and spending in both observation orders. R8-F2 concerns a target that stays in memory and reaches a different retirement guard.

A blocked native proposal no longer sets the maximum candidate distance. The recorded restricted-travel case selects and strikes the farther admissible target. With both candidates blocked, the proposal is refused and neither receives a delivery.

The selector now requires cached rider sight for a held rider as well as stationary mounted-strike admission. In the recorded in-range cases, the farther target was struck when only it passed cached sight. The nearer target was struck with both clear and in the mount-only restriction control. R8-F1 concerns the separate native action-range requirement.

Restricted proposals still construct strike probes for candidates of unrelated ranks. The extra work is documented, and the record establishes neither a selection error nor a measured frame-time impact from it.

The remaining required corrections concern real-time automatic target selection and invalidation reporting.
